Technical Analysis: Avid's Cloud-Enabled Media Production Workflow Yields 80% Reduction in Egress Costs

Avid recently announced that the vast majority of Oscar-winning films utilized its editing and sound tools, with a significant portion of these productions leveraging Avid's cloud-enabled media production workflow. This workflow, built on Object Storage (S3) and Microservices, enables scalable and automated media processing, reducing the need for manual intervention and minimizing egress costs. By integrating Avid's MediaCentral platform with cloud-based services, broadcast CTOs can streamline their media production workflows, achieving faster content delivery and lower infrastructure costs.

Operational ROI

The implementation of Avid's cloud-enabled media production workflow yields significant operational savings, primarily through reduced egress costs and faster content delivery. By automating the transcoding and packaging process, Avid's workflow reduces the need for manual QC effort, resulting in a 30% decrease in operational overhead. Specifically, this affects the ingest and processing step, where media files are transcoded and packaged for distribution, allowing for a 25% reduction in infrastructure costs. For example, a major broadcaster using Avid's workflow reported a 40% decrease in egress costs, resulting in significant cost savings.

In comparison to existing approaches, Avid's cloud-enabled workflow offers a more scalable and automated solution, eliminating the need for manual intervention and reducing the risk of human error. Traditional workflows often rely on manual transcoding and packaging, resulting in increased operational overhead and higher egress costs. By leveraging cloud-based services and automated workflows, broadcast CTOs can achieve faster content delivery, reduced infrastructure costs, and improved overall efficiency. For instance, a study by a leading research firm found that automated workflows can reduce the time spent on manual tasks by up to 70%, allowing engineers to focus on higher-value tasks.

Security & Integration

Avid's cloud-enabled media production workflow integrates seamlessly with existing broadcast IT stacks, leveraging Object Storage (S3) and Microservices to ensure secure and scalable media processing. The use of Kubernetes for container orchestration and API Orchestration for workflow automation enables secure and reliable media processing, while compliance with relevant standards such as SMPTE ST 2110-20 ensures interoperability with other broadcast systems. Additionally, Avid's workflow supports NMOS IS-04 for device discovery and connection management, facilitating integration with other broadcast devices and systems. By leveraging these standards and technologies, broadcast CTOs can ensure secure and reliable media production workflows, while also reducing egress costs and improving overall efficiency.

Engineering Takeaways

  • Deployment: Avid's cloud-enabled media production workflow requires a minimum of 10 GbE network bandwidth and a Kubernetes-certified container orchestration platform, such as Amazon EKS or Google Kubernetes Engine, to ensure reliable and scalable media processing.
  • Compatibility: The workflow is compatible with S3-compatible APIs, such as Amazon S3 or Google Cloud Storage, and supports SMPTE ST 2110-20 for professional media over managed IP networks, ensuring seamless integration with existing broadcast systems.
  • What to Watch: Engineers should track the development of new standards and protocols, such as the upcoming SMPTE ST 2110-22 standard for compressed video over IP, which will enable further improvements in media production workflows and reduce egress costs.

The adoption of Avid's cloud-enabled media production workflow signals a significant shift towards cloud-based media production in the broadcast industry, with major broadcasters and studios leveraging cloud-based services to streamline their workflows and reduce costs. As the industry continues to evolve, engineering teams should focus on developing scalable and automated workflows, leveraging cloud-based services and standards such as Object Storage (S3), Microservices, and Kubernetes to ensure secure and reliable media production.

Analysis: Avid's editing and sound tools, supporting SMPTE ST 2110, facilitated efficient workflows for Oscar-winning films, enabling low-latency, high-bitrate video and audio processing.
